# Obed Abernethy

## Overview

- **Age:** 60 (at the start of the novel)  <sub>[v1 c1 P23](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0023), [v1 c2 P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c1 P6](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0006), [v1 c2 P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v1 c37 P16](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0016)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c1 P2](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0002), [v1 c1 P5](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** farmer  <sub>[v1 c1 P2](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0002), [v1 c1 P6](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0006), [v1 c3 P30](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0030)</sub>

## Appearance

Obed was an unusual-appearing man with an awkward frame, hunching shoulders, and lengthy iron-gray hair. He possessed warm brown eyes that shone with satisfaction when pleased, and from the age of twenty he continuously wore a thick, gentle brown beard.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003), [v1 c32 P34](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0034)_

## Personality

Extremely shy, timid, and taciturn, Obed rarely left his home and almost never spoke unless spoken to, preferring to listen quietly to loquacious companions. Despite his bashfulness, he was deeply tender-hearted, soft-hearted, and wise, showing immense patience and good nature. When he set his mind on something, he possessed a quiet, powerful stubbornness that he maintained without raising his voice.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P2](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0002), [v1 c1 P4](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0004), [v1 c2 P27](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0027), [v1 c4 P21](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0021), [v1 c14 P49](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0049), [v1 c27 P4](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0004)_

## History

Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza. Facing advancing age, poor health, and a shortage of farm labor, he and Thirza arranged to adopt a young boy from an asylum. When Obed drove to Alder River station to collect the child, he discovered that an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent by mistake; unable to tell her the truth, he brought her home. Though he was notoriously afraid of young girls, he quickly became fond of Nell and quietly insisted on keeping her. Over the next four years, Obed formed a deep friendship with Nell, encouraging her studies and taking immense pride in her accomplishments, including her winning of the Avery scholarship. He eventually passed away, leaving Nell and Thirza grieving his loss.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P6](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0006), [v1 c1 P23](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0023), [v1 c2 P17](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0017), [v1 c2 P27](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0027), [v1 c4 P21](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0021), [v1 c6 P37](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0037), [v1 c24 P17](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0017), [v1 c30 P38](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0038), [v1 c36 P41](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0041), [v1 c37 P16](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0016)_
